subject: Egress Strict Mode: connector allowlist & firewall exceptions

Subject: Private endpoint deploy - allowlist & firewall ask

Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're ready to stand up Redwood Private in our staging VPC but security requires a tight egress allowlist and a short justification for any required firewall exceptions. Can you confirm the IPs and ports we should open from our NATed subnet to the Redwood control plane and any third-party endpoints?

We're trying to avoid a blanket 0.0.0.0/0 egress rule. Also, does Redwood need any inbound holes from our side or is the connection entirely outbound?

Attached is our partial network diagram for context.

Best,
Lenora
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer
Zephyr Health

Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy - allowlist & firewall ask

Lenora — thanks for the diagram. Quick summary before I loop in infra:

- Redwood Private connects outbound from your private deployment to our control plane (TLS over 443). No inbound public ports are required on your workload nodes.
- For strict-mode egress (preferred), you can allow only the specific Redwood control-plane IP ranges and a few third-party endpoints (package repos, metrics ingestion).
- We recommend routing through your corporate NAT/proxy; if you do NAT, we need the stable NAT IP(s) you will source from so we can bind them to the tenant. If you use a forward proxy, please provide the proxy FQDN and cert details.

Connor — can you draft the exact IPs/ports and note any exceptions for updates/health-checks? Tessa, add anything about our recommended retry/fallback behavior for blocked egress.

I attached a current egress IP report that lists the control-plane and telemetry ranges.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
--

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Lenora Cho <lenora.cho@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy - allowlist & firewall ask

Lenora / Marissa — draft allowlist and notes below. This is intended for strict-mode (minimal outbound) deployments.

Allowlist (egress from Zephyr staging VPC to Redwood):
- 34.201.12.8/29 (Redwood control-plane API, TLS 443)
- 34.201.12.16/28 (Telemetry ingestion, TLS 443)
- 52.24.78.128/26 (Model artifacts CDN, HTTPS 443)
- 18.205.93.0/24 (Package & OS repo mirror, HTTPS 443)

Ports: 443 outbound only. ICMP and DNS (UDP 53/TCP 53) allowed to your internal resolvers. If you intentionally force egress via a corporate HTTP proxy, allow outbound to the proxy on its listening port and provide us the proxy IP and the client cert CN used for mTLS.

Notes and exceptions:
- Kernel-level TCP connection timeouts can cause long-lived streams to drop. We recommend 15min idle timeout on NAT gateways for client->server streams to avoid unexpected truncation of model responses.
- If Zephyr plans to use per-request streaming for long responses, please allow the SYN/ACK keepalive and TCP window scaling (no DPI that terminates TLS).
- We will provide fallback behavior: if a control-plane endpoint is unavailable, we failover to the secondary IP range above. Please ensure both ranges are routable from your NAT.

We do not require any inbound rules opened to your cluster. All work is initiated outbound by your agents.

Naomi — can you confirm any Palo Alto IPS/APP-ID signatures we should expect to see and provide a one-pager for their SOC team?

Connor O'Brien
Infra Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Lenora Cho <lenora.cho@zephyrhealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: paloalto-support@paloaltonetworks.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2027 11:27:00 -0800

Connor — appreciate the precise ranges. A couple of follow-ups from our SOC review:

- Can you provide a signed Acceptable Use Policy addendum stating Redwood will not attempt outbound connections to other Zephyr hosts from the private deployment? We need that for our change approval.
- Our perimeter team asks for a list of observable indicators (SNI, certificate CNs, HKPs) so they can create APP-ID and SSL-decrypt exceptions only for the needed flows.
- We will publish the NAT IPs on Friday when the staging NAT assignment is complete.

If you can supply the one-pager and the AUP addendum, we can greenlight a limited rollout next week.

Thanks,
Lenora
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lenora Cho <lenora.cho@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy - allowlist & firewall ask

Lenora — good plan. Deliverables attached:

- Signed AUP addendum (signed-aup.pdf)
- Network diagram (network-diagram-v2.pdf) with annotated egress routes and NAT-binding notes
- One-page APP-ID/SSL guidance (inline summary & attached CSV for SNI/fingerprint checks)

Next steps:
1) You publish the staging NAT IPs and we will bind them to your tenant (we will not accept dynamic / ephemeral source addresses).
2) Once your perimeter team applies the allowlist and APP-ID exceptions, we will kick off a short canary deploy to validate connection stability.
3) If streaming performance looks good we move to a broader staging sweep.

Connor flagged the 15-minute idle timeout recommendation and the TLS keepalive guidance above — please confirm with your infra team. If Zephyr prefers a proxy approach instead of NAT, share the proxy FQDN and cert CN and we'll validate mTLS config.

Happy to hop on a quick live call with your SOC and perimeter folks tomorrow at 10am PT to walk the one-pager.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
